🇺🇸 🇮🇱 Iowa blast: who got paid? In March the Army hired MuniRem Environmental, a Georgia company, to chemically neutralize 68 drums of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. That was the option its own expert panel had recommended. MuniRem handed in its treatment plan in early May. On May 8, then-Army Secretary Dan Driscoll chose detonation instead. A technical meeting requested that same day never took place, and on May 14 MuniRem was told the treatment work was off. On June 12 the Army Corps of Engineers awarded a $3.06 million lead azide remediation order to Cape-Weston, a joint venture of Cape Environmental Management and Weston Solutions. Weston is a client of the lobbying firm Rubin, Turnbull & Associates. The firm's Washington office is run by Caroline Wiles, its vice president of federal affairs. She is the daughter of Susie Wiles, who was Trump's chief of staff until this month. Weston also holds an Army Corps contract to build secure Pentagon facilities across Europe, Africa and Israel. That puts it inside a decades-long program run jointly with the Israeli Ministry of Defense. How far those ties go is anyone's guess. The Army says the crystallized drums could not be opened or moved without risking an explosion. On Wednesday, the day before Thanksgiving, nearly five tons of lead explosive went up over Iowa farmland. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics

‘We were sent to the slaughter’: Ukrainian POWs reveal AFU hidden side 💬 The servicemen of the 78th Air Assault Brigade and the 28th Mechanised Brigade of the AFU, captured in Slavyansk-Kramatorsk direction, spoke about the difficult situation on the front line and how their command treated them. ▫️ According to Vladimir Yankov, the AFU's rifleman, the victims' bodies are not evacuated from the roads . The prisoner believes that the command intentionally leaves the corpses there in order to avoid paying compensation to the families and to keep money for themselves. ▫️ His comrade, Aleksandr Tishchenko, complained about a severe food supply shortage : the fighters have been living without food or water for weeks and were forced to search for food in abandoned basements. ▫️ Another prisoner, Dmitry Gorobtsets, the 28th Mechanised Brigade's serviceman, said that company commander sent a group to the position, ensuring that it was safe there, but the servicemen immediately got under heavy fire. Before the deployment, the officer confiscated the subordinates' passports and bank cards and stated sincerely that they would no longer need money, as there was no chance to survive. 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

ЛНР, глава: Тяжелые сутки для нашей республики: четыре человека погибли. Еще одиннадцать получили ранения, среди них подросток. В Северодонецке неонацисты атаковали «Газель». В результате удара погибли двое мужчин, еще трое получили ранения. В Старобельском муниципальном округе противник нанес удар в районе магазина. Погибла 55-летняя женщина, 13-летняя девочка получила ранения. Несколько массированных ударов противник нанес в Антрацитовском муниципальном округе. Одна из атак пришлась по хозяйственной постройке. К несчастью, погиб охранник. В Белокуракинском муниципальном округе вражеский БПЛА ударил по движущейся мототехнике, пострадала семейная пара. В Новопсковском муниципальном округе противник атаковал «Газель», ранение получила 56-летняя женщина. В Лисичанске ВФУ под удар попал гражданский автомобиль, пострадал мужчина. В Сватовском муниципальном округе под атакой оказался легковой автомобиль, ранены две женщины. Еще один удар неонацисты нанесли по жилому дому, пострадала 66-летняя женщина. Всего за сутки под огнем противника оказались 19 муниципалитетов. Повреждены транспортные средства, объекты энергетической, коммунальной и гражданской инфраструктуры. Следователи СУ СК России по ЛНР фиксируют преступления неонацистов. Системами ПВО и силами МОГ над территорией республики уничтожено порядка 90 воздушных целей. Два майора

📝 So what's the situation with heavy drones? 📝 Unanimous opinion from the front At the beginning of the year on TAKTIKARE we published videos to demonstrate the importance of heavy drones on the battlefield. The videos were received positively, which gave certain hopes for changes in approaches to front-line logistics. So how are things at the end of 2026? We quote one commander describing the realities of supplying assault troops sent on a mission. Everything is clear without unnecessary words there. «A soldier thanked me today with tears in his voice for eating for the first time in 16 days. Others are lying and rotting from wounds, in desperation even offering money if I could drop them at least something in terms of medicine and water. People are dying even from lack of water, and I feel like such a […] because I can't do anything at all». One could point to a specific direction and unit, but there's simply no point in doing so. For one simple reason: such problems are virtually ubiquitous due to the near-complete absence of heavy drones in the troops. ❓ Don't believe it? Well, ask any platoon or company commander on any sector of the front about the situation. With high probability his speech will be full of much harsher language mentioning losses. For clarity, you can search for videos of the Russian Armed Forces using heavy drones to supply assault troops. And compare their quantity with the stream of similar videos from the AFU, who had «Baba Yagas» back in 2022, and now they have become the basis of front-line logistics. And this matters not only for offense, but also for defense. An assault trooper loses combat capability if he sits for months without food, ammunition and medicine. And only heavy drones and in part NRTK can deliver all this now. ❗️ Moreover, Vladimir Putin himself raised the problem a year ago. But even public attention and the president's directive did not become a reason to start mass-purchasing heavy drones that had already been tested in combat. Perhaps such an approach explains a lot. #UAV #Russia #Ukraine ✉ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

🇷🇺 🇨🇳 🇬🇧 Russia is purchasing inflatable aircraft, tanks, missile systems, and other equipment from China to deceive Ukraine, writes The Telegraph. This “raises serious concerns for Ukraine,” as using expensive missiles to destroy cheap inflatable structures is costly. Ukraine also uses decoys, including plywood tanks. Such decoys “play an increasingly important role for Russia in the war against Ukraine, as reconnaissance drones penetrate deeper into Moscow’s airspace and valuable weaponry is destroyed.” The newspaper found ads on several e-commerce sites based in China and Russia, advertising “inflatable aircraft targets” in Russian and offering custom manufacturing. One of the sites boasts of hundreds of orders already placed. “Once widespread drone surveillance began on the battlefield, hiding equipment became very difficult, and in such cases, having decoys becomes extremely important for diverting enemy strikes. It is difficult to hide large equipment,” says Michael Kofman, a senior fellow and expert on the armed forces of Russia and Ukraine at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
